----Petitioners  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp 2. Smt. Jafra W/o Mubarik, D/o Yunus, R/o Ward No. 22,
 Village Phephana, Tehsil Nohar, District Hanumangarh.
 ----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Vikas Bijarnia For Respondent(s) : Mr. Abhishek Purohit, A.G.A.
Present in person : Ms. Jafra - respondent No.2  Mr. Mubarik - petitioner No.1  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE FARJAND ALI Order 15/05/2024 1.

The instant criminal misc. petition has been filed under Section 482 of Cr.PC for quashing of FIR No.91/2023 registered at Police Station Phephana, District Hanumangarh for the offences Mubarik vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:21993) on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9885293/
1
354, 354(B), 34, 342 of IPC, Section 67 of IT Act and Section 27 of Arms Act.

2. It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that the dispute in between the parties has been resolved through an amicable settlement and now, there remains no controversy in between them and the parties do not wish to continue the criminal proceedings further.

3. On the other hand, complainant-respondent No.2; who is present in person and has been identified by her husband i.e. petitioner No.1-Mubarik, who is also present in person and has been identified by his counsel Mr. Vikas Bijarnia; admits the fact of compromise and submits that she is willing if the FIR and the proceedings are quashed on the basis of compromise entered in between the parties.
4.

In support of the above contentions, a copy of the application dated 06.04.2024 submitted by the complainant-respondent No.2 before the Investigating Officer is furnished before this Court for perusal.
5. Learned Additional Government Advocate has opposed the petition.

However, he has submitted the factual report dated 10.05.2024, along with a copy of application dated 06.04.2024 submitted by the complainant-respondent No.2 before the Investigating Officer, wherein it is mentioned that the complainant-respondent No.2 wants to drop all the proceedings arising out of the impugned FIR.

6. Heard, perused the material available on record more particularly the police report, copy of the application of the [2024:RJ-JD:21993] (3 of 4) [CRLMP-4362/2023] complainant-respondent No.2, nature of allegation and considered the factum of compromise.
The parties to the lis have resolved their dispute amicably and do not wish to continue the criminal proceedings and have jointly prayed for quashing of the same.

7. Initially, the impugned FIR has been lodged against the petitioners for several offences including the offence under Section 376 of IPC, however, during the course of investigation, the police have found the offences under Sections 498-A, 406 and 323 of IPC proved against the petitioners.

8. Some of the offences alleged in this matter are non-compoundable, however, Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab reported in [(2012) 10 SCC 303] has propounded that if it is convinced that offences are entirely personal in nature and do not affect the public peace or tranquility and where it feels that quashing of such proceedings on account of compromise would bring about peace and would secure ends of justice, the High Court should not hesitate to quash the same by exercising the inherent powers vested in it.

entities.text: Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab reported in [(2012) 10 SCC 303]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is observed that in such cases, the prosecution becomes a lame prosecution and pursuing such a lame prosecution would be a waste of time and energy that will also unsettle the compromise and obstruct restoration of peace.

This court is aptly guided by the principles propounded by Hon'ble the Supreme Court and feels that where the dispute is essentially inter se between the parties, either they are relatives, neighbours or having business relationship and which does not affect the society at large, then in such cases, with a view to Mubarik vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:21993) on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9885293/
2 maintain harmonious relationships between the two [2024

[CRLMP-4362/2023] sides, to end-up the dispute in between them permanently as well as for restitution of relationship, the High Court should exercise its inherent power to quash the FIR and all other subsequent proceedings initiated thereto.

9. Here in this case, though some of the offences are not compoundable but the parties have settled the dispute amicably and that is essentially in between the parties which is not affecting public peace and tranquility, therefore, with a view to maintain the harmony and to resolve the dispute finally in between the parties, it is deemed appropriate to quash the FIR and all further proceedings undertaken in pursuance thereof.
10. Accordingly, the criminal misc. petition is allowed and the FIR mentioned above, and all further proceedings undertaken in pursuance thereof are hereby quashed and set aside.
11. The factual report dated 10.05.2024 as well as copy of application dated 06.04.2024 be placed on record.
12. The stay petition is disposed of.
(FARJAND ALI),J Abhishek Kumar S.No.643 Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
